serif.purpose: Anything the user reads as content: note titles wherever they appear, page titles, section headings, and the rendered/edited note body itself. Never used for interface chrome.

sans.purpose: All interactive chrome: buttons, badges, form controls, nav, generic dialog/sheet/card titles. The default UI voice.

mono.purpose: Code blocks, inline code, CodeMirror editor content, API token display, JSON import preview. System monospace stack, no custom webfont.

shadows.name: floating-overlay
shadows.purpose: Popover, select dropdown, and combobox dropdown — always paired with ring-1 ring-foreground/10. Never used on docked/inline surfaces like cards or dialogs.

shadows.name: ambient-sidebar
shadows.purpose: The sidebar's rare floating variant and the inset main-content area — a softer touch than the overlay shadow.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default button variant — moss-green fill, used for the main affirmative action on a page or dialog.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.25rem; height: 1.75rem; padding: 0 0.5rem; border-radius: 0.6rem; border: 1px solid transparent; font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1.625; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary, oklch(0.5 0.1 150)); color: var(--primary-foreground, oklch(0.99 0.01 140)); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary, oklch(0.5 0.1 150)) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring, oklch(0.62 0.09 150)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.62 0.09 150)) 30%, transparent); outline: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Pale-sage fill for secondary actions alongside a primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: var(--secondary, oklch(0.96 0.015 140)); color: var(--secondary-foreground, oklch(0.32 0.03 150)); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--secondary, oklch(0.96 0.015 140)), var(--foreground, oklch(0.22 0.02 150)) 5%); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Transparent at rest, filled with a muted tint on hover — the low-emphasis action button.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.22 0.02 150)); border-color: var(--border, oklch(0.89 0.02 140)); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--input, oklch(0.89 0.02 140)), transparent 50%); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Low-opacity red fill rather than a solid red button — restrained semantic color, matching the badge system's treatment.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)), transparent 90%); color: var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)), transparent 80%); }

components.name: Difficulty Badge
components.description: Pill-shaped status chip — the system's primary carrier of semantic color. This instance shows the 'hard' difficulty variant; easy/medium/good/again follow the same shape with emerald/amber/blue/red tints respectively.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 1.25rem; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 0.625rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-badge-hard { background: color-mix(in oklch, oklch(0.63 0.2 25), transparent 85%); color: oklch(0.5 0.2 25); }

components.name: Outline Badge (tag chip)
components.description: Interactive tag/project chip — outline variant, clickable, filters the note list on click.
components.css: .ds-badge-outline { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--input, oklch(0.89 0.02 140)), transparent 80%); color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.22 0.02 150)); border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.89 0.02 140)); cursor: pointer; } .ds-badge-outline:hover { background: var(--muted, oklch(0.96 0.015 140)); }

components.name: Note Card
components.description: Signature component: fixed-height card so grid rows stay aligned regardless of content length, with a stretched-link title and a bottom gradient fade signaling clipped overflow.
components.html:
Segment tree

Range queries in O(log n)...

components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 18rem; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 0.75rem; background: var(--card, oklch(0.99 0.006 145)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--foreground, oklch(0.22 0.02 150)), transparent 90%); font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1.625; } .ds-card-header { padding: 1rem 1rem 0; } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'Literata Variable', serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.22 0.02 150)); } .ds-card-content { position: relative; flex: 1; min-height: 0; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; overflow: hidden; font-family: 'Literata Variable', serif; } .ds-card-fade { position: absolute; inset-inline: 0; bottom: 0; height: 2rem; background: linear-gradient(to top, var(--card, oklch(0.99 0.006 145)), transparent); pointer-events: none; } .ds-card-footer { padding: 0 1rem 1rem; display: flex; gap: 0.375rem; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Compact translucent-fill input, the default form control across the app.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 1.75rem; width: 100%; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 0.6rem; border: 1px solid var(--input, oklch(0.89 0.02 140)); background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--input, oklch(0.89 0.02 140)), transparent 80%); font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.22 0.02 150)); outline: none; transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.53 0.03 150)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring, oklch(0.62 0.09 150)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.62 0.09 150)) 30%, transparent); }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Flat icon+label nav item; active state fills with the sage sidebar-accent token and adds medium weight.
components.html: Home
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; width: 100%; padding: 0.5rem; border-radius: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--sidebar-foreground, oklch(0.22 0.02 150)); text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--sidebar-accent, oklch(0.96 0.015 140)); } .ds-nav-item-active { background: var(--sidebar-accent, oklch(0.96 0.015 140)); font-weight: 500; color: var(--sidebar-accent-foreground, oklch(0.32 0.03 150)); }

narrative.overview:
Note and Learn is a single-user tool, not a marketing surface, and its design reads that way on purpose: a compact, olive-and-paper working notebook rather than a SaaS dashboard. The neutral scale is never true gray — background, borders, and text all carry a faint moss tint from the same ~150° hue family that the primary accent lives in, so the whole interface feels like it was cut from one material instead of a gray shell with a brand color dropped on top. Surfaces sit flat against that paper-toned background, separated by hairline rings rather than shadows; shadow is reserved for the handful of things that genuinely float above the page (popovers, selects, comboboxes).

Density is deliberately tight — 28px controls, 12px base UI text, compact spacing — because this is a tool its one user operates dozens of times a day, not a surface meant to feel spacious for a first-time visitor. The one real extravagance is typographic: everything the user actually reads as content (a note's title, a page's title, a section heading, the note body itself) switches to a serif face, while every piece of interactive chrome (buttons, badges, dialogs, generic component titles) stays in the sans UI face. That split is the system's signature — it's what makes scanning a grid of technical notes feel like reading a notebook page instead of scrolling a form.
keyCharacteristics: One accent hue (~150°, moss/olive) carries primary, ring, and sidebar-primary; neutrals share its tint rather than being true gray.
Flat-by-default: hairline ring (ring-1 ring-foreground/10) defines containers; shadow is reserved for floating overlays.
Serif (Literata) for anything read as content; sans (Inter) for interactive chrome — never mixed within the same role.
Dense, compact control sizing (28px controls, 12px base text) suited to a power-user tool used many times a day.
Pill-shaped badges carry all semantic status color (difficulty, recall rating, tags, project) rather than color on text or backgrounds elsewhere.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: Every neutral and the primary accent share one hue family (~140–150°). A new UI color that isn't a deliberate semantic break (destructive red, difficulty/rating chips) should be a lightness/chroma step within that family, not a new hue.

rules.name: The Reading Serif Rule
rules.body: Anything the user reads as content — a note's title wherever it appears, a page title, a section heading inside a content list — renders in Literata. Anything that is interface chrome around that content — dialogs, sheets, alerts, generic Card titles, buttons, badges — stays in Inter. Never mix the two within the same role.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface docked in the normal document flow (card, dialog, sidebar) gets a ring, never a shadow. Shadow is earned only by floating above unrelated content.

dos: Do keep every note-facing title (card, detail page, table row, page header) in Literata serif; keep every piece of surrounding interface chrome in Inter sans.
Do define container depth with a hairline ring (ring-1 ring-foreground/10) at rest; add shadow-md only when a surface floats above unrelated page content (popover, select, combobox).
Do carry semantic status (difficulty, recall rating, tags) as badge fills, not colored text or full-color solid backgrounds elsewhere.
Do keep new UI colors within the existing ~140–150° hue family unless the need is a genuine semantic break like destructive red.
Do compensate for the deliberately compact (20–32px) control sizing with the (pointer: coarse) media query rather than growing controls for every user.
donts: Don't add a second UI accent hue; route new emphasis through moss-green at a different lightness/chroma, or through the established destructive/difficulty/rating palettes.
Don't put shadows on resting cards, dialogs, or the docked sidebar — that breaks the flat-by-default elevation model this system is built on.
Don't render note titles or page titles in the sans/heading font, or generic dialog/component chrome in serif — the two faces are role-locked, not a stylistic mix-and-match.

Don't treat this as a marketing/persuade surface (no hero imagery, no decorative illustration, no gradient-heavy visual language) — it's a personal utility tool and its restraint is intentional, not a placeholder waiting for "real" design.
